docs.explain: DAYS and a plain subtraction answer the same question, and they answer it differently enough to matter. DAYS takes the end date first, so the answer is positive and the formula says which end is which. `C2-B2` is a difference that reads backwards the moment somebody fills it down a column the wrong way. The unit is days and only days. Turning that into weeks is ordinary arithmetic on the result, because a date is a number and everything you know about numbers applies to it. That is why date maths works at all. Adding thirty to a date gives the date thirty days later, subtracting one date from another gives the gap in days, and dividing the gap by seven gives weeks. Excel will even format the answer of a date plus a number as a date, which is the fastest way to build a due date from a term length. The trap is that a serial means nothing on its own. 45352 is only 1 March 2024 because somebody agreed on 1899 as the epoch. A cell holding a day count must never be formatted as a date, or it will claim to be a Tuesday in 1900.
